# Spatial Point Patterns

## Exercise 11.1 {-}

After loading **spatstat**, recreate the plot obtained by `plot(longleaf)` 
by using **ggplot2** and `geom_sf()`, and by `sf::plot()`.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
library(spatstat)
library(sf)
plot(longleaf) # spatstat plot

# using sf::plot() :
ll = st_as_sf(longleaf)
box = ll[1,]
pts = ll[-1,]
st_geometry(box) |> plot() #cex = 2*marks/max(marks))
marks = pts$spatstat.geom..marks.x
st_geometry(pts) |> plot(cex = 2*marks/max(marks), add = TRUE)

# using ggplot2:
library(ggplot2)
pts$marks = marks
ggplot() + geom_sf(data = box) + geom_sf(data = pts, aes(size = marks))
# how to get open circles? use geom_point():
p = as.data.frame(st_coordinates(pts))
ggplot() + geom_sf(data = box) + geom_point(aes(x = X, y = Y), data = p, shape = 1, size = 10 * marks / max(marks))
```

## Python

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
import shapely
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_map, geom_point, theme_minimal

# the longleaf data from spatstat: tree locations in a 200 x 200 m window,
# marks are tree diameters (exported from R to data/longleaf.csv)
ll = pd.read_csv("data/longleaf.csv")
box = gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=[shapely.box(0, 0, 200, 200)])

# matplotlib: open circles, size proportional to the marks
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((0, 0), 200, 200, fill=False))
ax.scatter(ll.x, ll.y, s=(20 * ll.marks / ll.marks.max()) ** 2,
           facecolors="none", edgecolors="black")
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.set_axis_off()
plt.show()

# plotnine, the ggplot2 equivalent: open circles with geom_point (shape="o")
(
    ggplot()
    + geom_map(box, fill=None)
    + geom_point(aes(x="x", y="y", size="marks"), data=ll, shape="o", fill="none")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```
:::

## Exercise 11.2 {-}

Convert the sample locations of the NO$_2$ data used in [Chapter
12](https://r-spatial.org/book/12-Interpolation.html) to a `ppp`
object, with a proper window.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
library(tidyverse) |> suppressPackageStartupMessages()
no2 <- read_csv(system.file("external/no2.csv", 
    package = "gstat"), show_col_types = FALSE)
library(sf)
crs <- st_crs("EPSG:32632")
st_as_sf(no2, crs = "OGC:CRS84", coords = 
	c("station_longitude_deg", "station_latitude_deg")) |>
	st_transform(crs) -> no2.sf
# read_sf("data/de_nuts1.gpkg") |> st_transform(crs) -> de
"https://github.com/edzer/sdsr/raw/main/data/de_nuts1.gpkg" |> 
  read_sf() |> 
  st_transform(crs) -> de
# create an observation window sf object that contains the same mark:
win = st_sf(NO2 = NA, geometry = st_union(st_geometry(de)))
rbind(win, no2.sf[,"NO2"]) |> as.ppp() -> p
plot(p)
```

## Python

```{python}
no2 = pd.read_csv("data/no2_stations.csv")  # from the gstat R package
no2_sf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    no2[["NO2"]],
    geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(no2.station_longitude_deg, no2.station_latitude_deg),
    crs="OGC:CRS84").to_crs("EPSG:32632")
de = gpd.read_file("data/de_nuts1.gpkg").to_crs("EPSG:32632")  # from edzer/sdsr

# observation window: union of the states; no Python equivalent of ppp exists
# in the packages used here, so we keep window, locations and marks together
win = de.geometry.union_all()

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
gpd.GeoSeries([win]).plot(ax=ax, facecolor="none", edgecolor="black")
no2_sf.plot(ax=ax, markersize=no2_sf.NO2 * 3, facecolor="none", edgecolor="red")
ax.set_axis_off()
plt.show()
```
:::

Alternatively, the `ppp` object can be created stepwise:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
st_union(st_geometry(de)) |> as.owin() -> w
st_geometry(no2.sf) |> as.ppp(W = w) -> p # requires sf 1.0-9
marks(p) = no2.sf$NO2
p
```

## Python

```{python}
p = {"window": win,
     "x": no2_sf.geometry.x.values,
     "y": no2_sf.geometry.y.values,
     "marks": no2_sf.NO2.values}
len(p["x"]), p["window"].geom_type, p["marks"][:5]
```
:::

## Exercise 11.3 {-}

Compute and plot the density of the NO$_2$ dataset, import the density as a `stars`
object and compute the volume under the surface. 

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
d = density(p)
plot(d)
library(stars)
st_as_stars(d) |> st_set_crs(crs) -> s
plot(s)
mean(s[[1]], na.rm = TRUE) * st_area(win)
```

## Python

```{python}
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter
from rasterio.features import geometry_mask
from rasterio.transform import from_origin
import rioxarray
import xarray as xr

# Gaussian kernel density estimate on a 128 x 128 grid over the window's
# bounding box, like spatstat::density(); sigma is the value spatstat picks by
# default (bw.diggle), 80073.65 m
sigma = 80073.65
xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax = win.bounds
n = 128
dx, dy = (xmax - xmin) / n, (ymax - ymin) / n
xc = xmin + dx * (np.arange(n) + 0.5)
yc = ymax - dy * (np.arange(n) + 0.5)
X, Y = np.meshgrid(xc, yc)

dens = np.zeros_like(X)
for px, py in zip(p["x"], p["y"]):
    dens += np.exp(-((X - px) ** 2 + (Y - py) ** 2) / (2 * sigma ** 2)) / (2 * np.pi * sigma ** 2)

inside = geometry_mask([win], out_shape=X.shape,
                       transform=from_origin(xmin, ymax, dx, dy), invert=True)
# spatstat applies a uniform edge correction by default: divide by the
# kernel mass that falls inside the window
edge = gaussian_filter(inside.astype(float), (sigma / dy, sigma / dx), mode="constant")
dens = np.where(inside, dens / edge.clip(1e-12), np.nan)

# as a georeferenced raster, like the stars object
s = xr.DataArray(dens, coords={"y": yc, "x": xc}, dims=("y", "x")).rio.write_crs("EPSG:32632")
s.plot()
plt.show()

np.nanmean(s.values) * win.area  # the volume under the surface
```
:::

this number is close to the number of observations, 

::: {.panel-tabset}
